_readme: SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for test-suite routing (master plan 2026-07-02, L1). Lives in hub git @ main; mirrored ONE-WAY to Firestore by .github/workflows/suites-deploy.yml — one doc per suite in `test-suites/{key}` + a slim meta doc `console-config/suites` (lane-1 lock 2026-07-03). The console reads the mirror (read-only); CI reads this file from its checkout. Edit HERE via PR — never in Firestore. Regenerate SUITES.md with: node scripts/gen-suites-doc.mjs

_fields.title/description: shown in the console Test Run dialog
_fields.config: the Playwright config the CI gate runs for this suite (already capture-appropriate)
_fields.capture: failure-only = screenshots/video only for failed tests (default) | all = every test (queue/journey owners' choice, L11)
_fields.specDir: spec root in this repo (run-isolated.sh SUITE_DIR)
_fields.appPaths: starlabs-angular globs — a branch diff matching any makes this suite MANDATORY
_fields.cfPaths: starlabs-cloud-function globs — same, for CF-side changes
_fields.areas: optional sub-routing within a suite: area name -> explicit spec list (run-isolated ONLY subset)
_fields.alwaysRun: true = baseline suite included in every routed run (none in v1; queue embeds its selftest baseline in each area list)
_fields.ciReady: false = local-only (no emulator config yet) — hidden from the console dialog
_fields.reviewNote: globs are a first draft — operator review pass pending (plan §7.4)

neutral._why: Files that are not app code. They never make a suite mandatory and never count as uncovered — a README commit must not read as 'untested'. Used by scripts/readiness (NOT by the console mirror, which only carries version/crossCutting/cfPredeploy). NOTE: `**/*.md` compiles to `^.*/[^/]*\.md$` and therefore requires a directory — root-level files need the bare `*.md` form too. Keep BOTH; do not 'simplify' this list. (globToRegex semantics are shared with console/functions/src/suites.ts and must not diverge.) Operator decision 2026-09-09 added: firebase.json + package-lock.json (config/lockfile — note package.json itself stays crossCutting, a dependency CHANGE still fans out to every suite), scripts/** (build/tooling, never shipped to a user), and 'src/app/LiveKit Cloud/**' (declared out of scope for automated coverage — this is the LiveKit Cloud component only; plain 'src/app/LiveKit/**' is NOT listed and still reports SUITES_MISSING). Operator decision 2026-09-09 also added *.spec.ts + **/*.spec.ts — Karma/Jasmine UNIT tests that ship to nobody and can never be driven by an e2e suite; 74 of the app's 425 were being counted as uncovered app code. (`profiles` carries a narrower `!**/*.component.spec.ts` exclusion which only applies inside its own matching; this is the global rule.) Also added: src/assets/** (vendored third-party binaries — MediaPipe .tflite/.wasm and friends; no Playwright suite can cover a wasm blob) and src/coi-serviceworker.js (vendored COI service worker). CSS added by operator decision 2026-09-08: stylesheets never make a suite mandatory. TRADE-OFF STATED AND ACCEPTED — a global stylesheet change can break layout on any screen, and this exempts ALL of it (a .css-only commit now reports NOT_APPLICABLE and would dispatch nothing). The trigger was src/app/app.component.css blocking a branch as 'uncovered': the app shell sits at the ROOT of src/app, where every suite's `src/app/<Folder>/**` glob fails to reach. Narrower alternatives (fencing only the shell, or adding the shell to crossCutting) were available and NOT chosen.

fenced._why: Areas that can NEVER be covered by an automated suite — a change there can only be validated by hand, so the readiness check reports NO_COVERAGE_POSSIBLE rather than pretending a suite could exist. ALSO consumed by scripts/check-route-coverage.mjs and scripts/check-atc-coupling.mjs, which drop these paths from the coverage denominator — one key, both toolchains. EMPTY as of 2026-09-08 (see _emptied below), so NO_COVERAGE_POSSIBLE is currently unreachable. Populate this list again if a genuinely un-automatable area appears; do NOT use it for code that merely lacks tests (that is SUITES_MISSING) or for dead code (that is `retired`).
fenced._emptied: OPERATOR DECISION 2026-09-08 — REVERSES the 2026-09-03/04 fencing. Removed: src/app/ATC/**, src/app/ATC-Ops/**, src/app/view-ai-generated-atc/**. Operator's reasoning, stated explicitly: the ATC restriction applies to the REAL database only; seeding into the emulator is allowed, so ATC components are not un-automatable. NOTE this narrows a rule previously recorded as absolute — starlabs-angular/CLAUDE.md:31 still reads 'Never read, write, or seed ATC Firestore collections… Exclude all src/app/ATC/** components and ATC readers from the test pipeline', and profiles/profilelist.spec.ts still cancels its Delete Profile case citing 'a standing rule, not an emulator limitation'. Those two records now CONTRADICT this key and should be updated, or a future session will re-fence these paths. CONSEQUENCES: (1) no suite claims src/app/ATC/**, so ATC changes now report SUITES_MISSING — still blocked, only the label and the reason change (operator acknowledged); (2) the second layer is untouched — _support/excluded-routes.ts (D-001) still stops any spec NAVIGATING to ~30 ATC routes, so removing this fence does NOT by itself permit ATC testing; (3) check-route-coverage and check-atc-coupling no longer subtract these paths, so ATC screens re-enter the coverage denominator and reported coverage will drop.

retired._why: DEAD routes: still registered in app.routes.ts but reachable only by typing the URL, and superseded by a live screen. They leave the coverage denominator because writing a spec for code that should be deleted is waste — but they are NOT `fenced`: fenced means an automated suite may never cover it (ATC, a hard constraint), whereas these COULD be tested and simply should not exist. Different reason, different remedy: the fix for an entry here is to delete the route and its component, at which point the entry goes too. Keyed by route with the evidence that it is dead.

routes./userprofile_old: Operator decision 2026-09-08. No reference anywhere in src/app outside its own component file; the sibling `/userprofile_old/:id` route is already commented out (app.routes.ts:38) and the live screen is /userprofile. Counted three times in coverage because `Participants Profile Management` is claimed by journey, modes AND profiles, so it inflated all three.
routes./devtestmic: Operator decision 2026-09-08. Module is literally src/app/Test Component; zero references anywhere in src/app outside app.routes.ts. NOTE: /routeconfiguration was proposed alongside it and REJECTED as dead — despite living in a folder named route-configuration-duplicate, it is linked from the app shell nav (app.component.html:101) for rolemanager/developer and read at app.component.ts:482. It is live and still needs a suite.

retired._appPathsWhy: FILE-PATH twin of `routes` above, added 2026-09-09 so the PUSH-TIME readiness check can see deprecation — it reads this key, never `routes`. Matched BEFORE `fenced` and before any suite, so a deprecated file is neither a coverage gap (SUITES_MISSING) nor manual-only (NO_COVERAGE_POSSIBLE): it simply does not participate, and a commit touching only deprecated files reports NOT_APPLICABLE and proceeds. Every entry here MUST correspond to a route in `routes` above — that is where the evidence of deadness lives. Remove BOTH when the component is deleted. 2026-09-09 — the two entries below are a SECOND kind of dead and deliberately have NO `routes` counterpart: openvidu-loading-game and authloading are not registered in app.routes.ts at all AND are referenced by nothing outside their own folder (verified: 0 external class references, 0 template uses of <app-openvidu-loading-game> / <app-authloading>). Unroutable and unreferenced is deader than a dead route, so the evidence lives here instead. CHECKED AND NOT RETIRED in the same pass: route-configuration-duplicate (3 external refs, though its class names collide with the live src/app/route-configuration — needs a human look), Test Component/DevTestMic, slackwebhookurls and arena-design-insights (all routed), and updatesnackbar (used by app.component.ts).

crossCutting._why: narrow map, broad fallback (preview-time-gate journal 2026-06-29): a match here can affect ANYTHING, so ALL ciReady suites become mandatory. Operator decision 2026-09-09 added the ROOT of src/app, which no suite glob could reach (every suite is shaped src/app/<Folder>/**): the app shell (app.component.*) and three app-wide root services. BUG FIX in the same pass — `src/app/**/*.guard.ts` compiles to ^src/app/.*/[^/]*\.guard\.ts$ and therefore REQUIRES a directory, so the two root guards (auth.guard.ts, role.guard.ts) never matched and were reported as uncovered rather than cross-cutting. The bare `src/app/*.guard.ts` form fixes it — exactly the `*.md` / `**/*.md` precedent documented in `neutral`. Keep BOTH forms. TRADE-OFF: a change to any of these now fans out to all 12 suites, which is expensive but is the safe direction for the app shell and the authorization gate. 2026-09-09 completed the sweep: src/main.ts (bootstrap), src/index.html (document shell), src/firebase-messaging-sw.js (FCM service worker), both app.*.server.ts (SSR config) and network-status.service.ts are now listed too, so no root-level file is left reporting as an uncovered feature.
crossCutting._sharedUi2026_09_09: loading-progress and ProfilePicture are SHARED UI: they live under profiles' appPaths but are imported by 9 systems each (measured, not assumed — loading-progress by queue/journey/support/events/appointments/content/business/workshops/comms; profile-picture by queue/journey/support/events/appointments/business/workshops/evomap/modes). Routing them to profiles alone meant a spinner change ran ONE gate while nine systems rendered it. They are NOT relocated to src/app/shared/** (operator decision 2026-09-09 — no file moves); listing them here gives the same routing without touching the tree. Narrower shared components (video-player, participants-analytics inputs, Product Designer delivery-set widgets, channel-communication) are deliberately NOT here: they are consumed by 1-4 named systems, so they are listed in those suites' appPaths instead, which is more precise than making every PR run everything.
